mutants.effect: Survival curves count patients who were still alive at last follow-up as deaths, so every curve drops too fast.
mutants.evidence: not ok 1 - with no competing event, cumulative incidence is exactly 1 − Kaplan–Meier, delayed entry included

mutants.effect: Patients stay in the at-risk group after they leave the study, so later deaths look rarer and curves sit too high.
mutants.evidence: not ok 1 - with no competing event, cumulative incidence is exactly 1 − Kaplan–Meier, delayed entry included

mutants.effect: The log-rank test overstates its variance when deaths are tied, so survival differences look less significant than they are.
mutants.evidence: not ok 1 - Freireich 6-MP vs placebo: chi2 = 16.79, p = 4.2e-5

mutants.effect: Fisher's exact test only counts tables in one direction, so mutual-exclusivity and enrichment p-values come out too small.
mutants.evidence: not ok 6 - Fisher's exact test: p in [0, 1], and the same for the table transposed or its rows swapped

mutants.effect: Multiple-testing correction skips a step, so a gene with a weaker p-value can be reported as more significant than a stronger one.
Hazard ratios handle patients who die on the same day with a cruder formula than the one the method states (Breslow, not Efron).
mutants.evidence: not ok 2 - mixed covariates, heavy ties — binary + unscaled age + a 3-level categorical; integer-month times put many deaths at the same time

mutants.effect: The t-test assumes both groups have the same spread when they do not, so p-values are wrong for unequal groups.
A cohort written as "A and B" contains everyone with A or B.
mutants.evidence: FAIL [msk_chord_2024] "A and B" is exactly the patients in both A and B  (A and B: engine 19,032, expected 6,241 (12791 extra, 0 missing))

mutants.effect: A cohort written as "A or B" contains only patients with both.
mutants.evidence: FAIL [msk_chord_2024] "A or B" is exactly the patients in either  (A or B: engine 6,241, expected 19,032 (0 extra, 12791 missing))

mutants.effect: Splitting a cohort into arms (KRAS G12C, then other KRAS, then wild-type) puts G12C patients in two arms at once.
mutants.evidence: FAIL [msk_chord_2024] the engine reports that the split's children add up to the parent  (0 + 916 + 2,194 + 7,809 = 10,919 of 7,809)

mutants.effect: A gene's frequency is divided by samples on the largest panel instead of samples whose panel actually covers that gene, so genes on smaller panels look rarer than they are.
mutants.evidence: FAIL nsclc_ctdx_msk_2022 mutations: PTEN  ours 77/52/2621 / cBioPortal 77/52/1257

mutants.effect: Whole-exome samples with two copy-number profiles are counted twice in the denominator, halving every copy-number frequency.
mutants.history: Shipped once: brca_tcga MYC amplification read 10.6% where cBioPortal says 21.2%.
mutants.evidence: FAIL brca_tcga copy number: MYC amplified  ours 229/229/2160 / cBioPortal 229/229/1080

mutants.effect: "TP53: MUT" also selects patients whose TP53 has only a copy-number change.
mutants.evidence: FAIL brca_tcga cohort: patients with a PIK3CA mutation (OQL "PIK3CA: MUT")  ours 352 / cBioPortal 317

mutants.effect: "Deeply deleted" also selects amplified patients, so a CDKN2A-loss cohort contains CDKN2A-amplified tumours.
mutants.evidence: FAIL nsclc_ctdx_msk_2022 cohort: patients with CDKN2A deeply deleted (OQL "CDKN2A: HOMDEL")  ours 137 / cBioPortal 136

mutants.effect: "APC: TRUNC_(1400-)" selects every APC truncation, so an N-/C-terminal split puts every truncated patient on the C-terminal side.

mutants.effect: "TP53: TRUNC" leaves out splice-site and start-loss mutations, which cBioPortal counts as truncating.

mutants.evidence: FAIL brca_tcga cohort: patients matching OQL "PIK3CA: TRUNC" (cBioPortal's mutations, its classes)  ours 2 / cBioPortal 3

mutants.effect: A risk group's mutation rate in Table 1 divides by every patient in the group, counting those whose panel never covered the gene as unmutated, so the rate reads too low.
mutants.evidence: not ok 1 - a patient whose panels omit the gene is not profiled, not unaltered; whole-exome covers every gene

mutants.effect: Table 1's q-values are corrected together with the rows the model was built from, whose tiny p-values are guaranteed, so every other row looks more significant than it is.
